name: Delhi Sultanate (Tughluq)

areaKm2.note: The world_1300 Sultanate of Delhi polygon measures 1.95 million km2 on the sphere (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1300.geojson, mid). The Delhi Sultanate infobox gives 1.5 million for 1300 (low) and 3.2 million for 1312 (high, with tributary Deccan); Seshat codes 2.8-3.2 million.

population.note: Educated guess. India had ~85 million in 1200 and 101-110 million in 1500 (Maddison 2001 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Sultanate); HYDE gives 123.7M for 1300 (OWID https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). The Sultanate directly ruled Punjab, the Gangetic plain, Gujarat, Malwa and Bengal (Deccan kings tributary), perhaps 35-50% of the subcontinent.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Delhi 200,000-400,000 (Seshat 135), Lahore, Multan, Gujarat ports.

activePersonnel.note: Historians state the Khalji Sultanate kept 300,000-400,000 cavalry and 2,500-3,000 war elephants as a standing army (Tripathi, Digby 1971 p. 24 via the Delhi Sultanate page), echoing Firishta's 475,000 horsemen (16th c., Alauddin Khalji page). The Catalan Atlas (1375) credits the sultan with 100,000 horsemen and 700 elephants (Tughlaq dynasty page). Mid: ~150,000 cavalry + ~80,000 infantry + support, after the 1320 civil war.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Iqta-holders' retainers and Hindu chiefs' contingents callable within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts (2 per elephant), siege engineers, the barid postal service and commissariat.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. A Turkic and Afghan military elite paid in cash and iqta, plus Hindu paik infantry; mass mobilisation of the peasantry was not the model.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Mounted archers of the iqta-holders and paid regulars.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: imported Central Asian and Arab horses, composite bows

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional mounted archers

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured household cavalry (khasakhail, largely of slave origin) and lancers (Delhi Sultanate page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: mail and lamellar, barded horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: elite household troops

count.note: Educated guess. Paik infantry, largely Hindu, for sieges and garrisons.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: light equipment

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: paid footmen

count.note: Catalan Atlas 700 (low, Tughlaq dynasty page) and 2,500-3,000 for the Khalji standing army (Digby 1971 via the Delhi Sultanate page, high); mid assumes losses in the 1320 succession war. Platform count.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: large royal elephant stables fed by tribute from the Deccan and Bengal

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: royal elephant establishment

count.note: Educated guess. Manjaniq (trebuchets) and arradas in siege trains (Chittor 1303, Ranthambore 1301).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Islamic-world trebuchets

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: siege specialists

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, a veteran of the Mongol wars, won the 1320 civil war; Khalji generals had beaten the Mongols 1298-1306

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: factional Turkic, Afghan and convert nobility; three dynastic changes 1290-1320

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: new dynasty after a civil war; long run of Deccan victories

weapons.note: Anchor: 4 (1250). Evidence: composite bows, trebuchets, high-quality steel blades

armor.note: Anchor: between 3 and 4. Evidence: mail and lamellar, barded horses for the elite

ships.note: Anchor: between 1 and 2. Evidence: river craft; Gujarat ports had merchant ships but no royal navy

fortification.note: Anchor: about 4. Evidence: Siri and Tughlaqabad walls, captured Rajput fortresses

logistics.note: Anchor: between 3 and 4. Evidence: Alauddin's price controls and state granaries, banjara grain carriers

communications.note: Anchor: 4 (relay horses). Evidence: barid relay post with horse and foot runners

isr.note: Anchor: between 3 and 4. Evidence: barid news-writers and spies

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has India only from 1600 (1,264) and China 1000 = 1,225, 1150 = 1,181; Egypt 1000 = 956, 1300 = 972 (2011 int$). Medieval South Asia placed in that band.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Land revenue taken at up to half the produce under Alauddin largely paid the army.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Doab and Punjab grain, heavily taxed.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Royal roads Delhi-Daulatabad, Delhi-Lahore-Multan, Delhi-Lakhnauti.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Gujarati and Bengali merchant shipping.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Cavalry armies campaigned 1,500 km into the Deccan (Warangal, Madurai) living partly off the land.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, banjara pack herds, camels in the west.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 row: fortified cities and summer heat against steppe invaders.

notes: Snapshot September 1320, when Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq took Delhi from Khusrau Khan; Warangal fell in 1323. Army figures in the sources (Firishta's 475,000, the 300,000-400,000 cavalry repeated on the Sultanate page) are chronicle-derived and taken as the high end; the mid is a composite with the Catalan Atlas figure. Population convention: directly ruled provinces; tributary Deccan kingdoms excluded. GDP per capita is a regional analogy. Personnel: active = cash-paid household and regular cavalry, paid paik infantry, royal elephants; trainedReserves = retainers of iqta-holders and Hindu chiefs' contingents; mobilizable = population x ratio.
